items.name: Big folders open faster
items.summary: File Explorer stops reading a folder's files to guess whether it holds pictures, music or documents, so folders with thousands of files open without a long wait.
items.effect: Folders no longer switch to a picture or music view on their own; you can still pick a view yourself. Folders you have already set a view for keep it.

items.name: Stuck apps do not hold up shutdown
items.summary: Shutdown, restart and sign-out stop waiting on apps that will not close. Apps that do not answer are closed after 5 seconds instead of 20.
items.effect: An app with unsaved work that is slow to answer is closed without asking. Save your work before you shut down.

items.name: Menus and windows respond sooner
items.summary: Menus open without their short pause, and windows minimize and maximize without animating.
items.effect: Windows lose their small fade and zoom animations.

items.name: Edge stays closed when closed
items.summary: Edge no longer starts quietly when you sign in and no longer keeps running after you close it, so fewer msedge.exe processes sit in memory.
items.effect: Edge takes a moment longer to open, and background notifications from Edge web apps stop. Edge also says “managed by your organization”, which is how it shows any policy. Applies the next time Edge starts.

items.name: No suggestions or promoted apps
items.summary: Windows stops suggesting apps and tips in Start, Settings and the lock screen, and stops quietly installing promoted apps for your account.
items.effect: You stop seeing Microsoft's tips and suggestions. Nothing you installed is removed.

items.name: No personalized ads in apps
items.summary: Apps can no longer use an advertising ID to show ads based on what you do, and Windows stops tailoring tips from your diagnostic data.
items.effect: You still see ads in apps that show them, just not personalized ones.

items.name: Start search without web results
items.summary: Searching from Start or the taskbar shows only your PC, apps and settings, with no Bing web suggestions mixed in. This is the “Web Searches” switch in Settings > Privacy & security > Search.
items.effect: You search the web from your browser instead. Microsoft Store suggestions in search are a separate switch and stay as they are. Only Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300.8697 and later) has this setting.

items.name: No activity history
items.summary: Windows stops recording which apps and files you open into an activity history and stops sending it to Microsoft.
items.effect: Features that continue what you were doing on another device, or list past activities, have nothing to show.

items.name: No promoted apps on new accounts
items.summary: Windows stops installing promoted apps and games on new accounts and after updates, for everyone who uses this PC.
items.effect: Nothing you use. Apps already installed stay.

items.name: Full right-click menu
items.summary: Right-clicking shows the full menu straight away, instead of Windows 11's short one with “Show more options”.
items.effect: You get the older, longer menu. The newer short menu is gone until you turn this off.

items.name: Pointer follows your hand exactly
items.summary: The pointer moves the same distance for the same hand movement, however fast you move the mouse (Enhance pointer precision off).
items.effect: Small, slow movements can feel less precise to some people. You can switch it back here any time.

items.name: No Sticky Keys pop-ups
items.summary: Pressing Shift five times, or holding Shift or Num Lock, no longer opens the Sticky Keys, Filter Keys or Toggle Keys prompt in the middle of a game or a document.
items.effect: The shortcuts that start these accessibility features stop working. The features themselves can still be turned on in Settings.

items.name: Show file endings
items.summary: File names show their real ending, so “invoice.pdf.exe” cannot pass for a PDF.
items.effect: Names are a little longer, and renaming a file lets you change its ending too, so take care when you rename.

items.name: End task from the taskbar
items.summary: Right-click an app on the taskbar and choose End task to close one that is stuck, without opening Task Manager.
items.effect: Nothing you would miss. End task closes the app without asking you to save.

items.name: Long file paths
items.summary: Apps that support it can open files whose full path is longer than 260 characters, instead of failing with “path too long”.
items.effect: Nothing you would miss. Older apps that do not support long paths keep their old limit.

items.name: Memory integrity off
items.summary: Turns off memory integrity (also called HVCI), which runs a security check on drivers inside a protected area. Games and other heavy apps run a few percent faster, up to about 8% in some tests.
items.effect: This lowers your protection. Memory integrity stops malware from loading harmful code into Windows itself, so leave it on unless you have tested that the speed matters to you. A company policy or a firmware lock can still keep it on. It takes effect after a restart, and Windows Security shows a warning while it is off.
sources: Tom's Hardware: Windows 11 VBS and HVCI gaming benchmarks
ComputerBase: VBS and HVCI in Windows 11, game benchmarks

items.name: Taskbar click opens the last window
items.summary: Clicking an app on the taskbar that has several windows open goes straight to the one you used last, instead of showing a row of previews first. Click again to go to the next window.
items.effect: You can still pick any window from the previews by hovering over the icon. This value is not documented by Microsoft, so a Windows update may stop honoring it.
sources: Windows Eleven Forum: Always use last active click on taskbar
NinjaOne: Last Active Click on the taskbar

items.name: File Explorer opens to This PC
items.summary: File Explorer opens showing your drives (This PC) instead of Home, which first has to gather your recent and cloud files.
items.effect: Home's recent and pinned files are no longer the first thing you see. They stay one click away in the sidebar.
sources: Windows Eleven Forum: Open File Explorer to This PC

items.name: File copies show the full details
items.summary: Copying or moving files shows the full progress window at once, with the speed graph and the time left, instead of a small box you have to open with “More details”.
items.effect: The progress window is a little taller. Nothing else changes.
sources: The value File Explorer itself saves when you open or close “More details”

items.name: No Game Bar pop-ups
items.summary: Pressing a controller's Xbox button or starting a game no longer opens Game Bar, or asks you to “get an app to open this ms-gamebar link” when Game Bar has been removed.
items.effect: Game Bar's controller button, clips and “record what happened” stop working. Other recorders, such as OBS, are not affected. The Quiet page has a separate, stronger switch that blocks game recording for everyone.

items.name: Full-quality wallpaper
items.summary: A JPEG picture you set as your wallpaper keeps its full quality instead of being compressed again, so gradients and dark pictures show less banding.
items.effect: Only pictures you set from now on are affected: set your wallpaper again after signing back in. The copy Windows keeps is a little larger.

items.name: No “finish setting up” pages or Explorer banners
items.summary: Stops the full-screen “Let's finish setting up your device” page after updates, and the OneDrive and Microsoft 365 banners at the top of File Explorer.
items.effect: Nothing you use. You can still finish setup from Settings, and OneDrive keeps syncing.
sources: Windows Eleven Forum: Let's finish setting up your device
Winaero: How to disable ads in Windows 11

items.name: Start keeps no recent files or app lists
items.summary: Start's Recommended section stops listing your recent files, recently added apps and most used apps, and stops showing tips and app suggestions. These are the switches in Settings > Personalization > Start, and they work on Windows 11 Home and Pro.
items.effect: Recent files also stop appearing in Jump Lists and in File Explorer's Recent list. Nothing is deleted, and Start's Pinned apps are not touched.
sources: Windows Eleven Forum: Recommended files in Start
Windows Eleven Forum: tips, shortcuts and new apps on Start

items.name: No maker apps for new devices
items.summary: Windows stops downloading the maker's companion app and custom icons when you plug in a mouse, keyboard, headset or monitor.
items.effect: The device itself still installs through Windows Update and works. If you want the maker's control app, you install it yourself. Applies to every user of this PC.
sources: Microsoft Learn: Prevent device metadata retrieval from the Internet

items.name: Shut down really shuts down
items.summary: Shut down turns the PC fully off. Normally Windows saves its running state to disk and resumes from it next time (Fast startup), so uptime never resets and driver, USB audio and dual-boot problems carry over.
items.effect: Starting the PC can take a few seconds longer, more on a hard drive than on an SSD. Restart already shuts Windows down fully, so only Shut down changes.
sources: Windows Settings (Power options > Turn on fast startup)
